title: Bind functional acceptance to verifiable evidence
cause: A controlled local clone of the 123-operation manifest with only descriptor PASS labels and matching counters, and zero evidence records, returns an empty releaseGate problems list. releaseGate checks declarations and counts, not the evidence that produced them. This is a release-integrity defect, not proof of an externally exploitable application endpoint.
decision: Introduce a qualified acceptance artifact, generated by the real execution harness and bound to the candidate and its dependencies. Validate content and provenance, not labels. Use the established CI artifact/attestation trust boundary rather than inventing a signing authority. A file hash alone does not authenticate an assertion.
steps: Define a versioned acceptance envelope containing stable operation/variant/role/chain/network keys, code and dependency revisions, configuration digest, specification revisions, run times, checkpoints where applicable, evidence-file SHA-256 digests and exclusions with evidence. Keep static registry declarations separate from execution results.

Extend the gate to load the envelope from an explicit allowed artifact root, reject absent files, traversal, symlink escape, hash mismatch, duplicate or missing required variants, stale revision/configuration bindings and fabricated counters. Require independently inspectable inputs, assertions, authoritative readback and consumer outcomes. Check referenced files without executing their contents.

Include chain and network in acceptance identity. Model actual acceptance environment separately from deployment network: Signet PASS plus a validated Mainnet configuration-difference record is valid; a Mainnet transaction is not required. Offline-only operations need their appropriate evidence kind, not an invented chain checkpoint.

Count all applicable inventory rows. Exclude only individually justified NOT APPLICABLE rows. A default-variant record must not implicitly qualify untested failure/recovery/UI variants. Preserve FAIL, BLOCKED and NOT TESTED truthfully.

Add adversarial tests for the saved label-only forgery, missing evidence, modified evidence, path escape, wrong network/revision/dependency, duplicate keys, omitted variants, unsupported exclusions, and a genuinely complete test-network fixture. Keep development --check separate.

node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js --runInBand --testPathPatterns=explorer-acceptance --cacheDirectory=<owned-cache>
acceptance: The saved forgery is rejected; real complete qualified Signet or justified Testnet evidence is accepted for a Mainnet candidate only with its independent configuration proof; every applicable operation and required variant is accounted for.
rollback: No database migration is justified by this finding. Version evidence readers additively; retain previously accepted artifacts for emergency rollback. Never disable the gate to release.

cause: The inspected release.sh and GitHub workflows contain no call to protocol-contract --release. CI invokes --check and production smoke --against. Existing authority preflight checks configured historical-readable protocols, which is not the required complete functional gate.
decision: Make evidence qualification an explicit precondition of candidate promotion and cutover, using the existing immutable-artifact, deployment-lock and rollback process. Do not deploy during preparation.
steps: Add a fail-closed acceptance-artifact verification step to the release artifact workflow and cmd_preflight before any release-affecting service, symlink, configuration or schema change. Pass the selected code/dependency/configuration identities explicitly; do not read acceptance from whichever old production instance happens to answer.

Make cmd_cutover reuse the same accepted artifact identity under the existing release lock, detecting changes since preflight. Verify the operator script itself matches the accepted candidate. Cover independently pinned gateway/frontend/backend/overlay component identities.

Preserve database backups and compatible migration ordering, private listener boundaries, owned upstreams and public routing. Deploy the accepted producer before compatible consumers. Remove only launch-blocking flags, not legitimate authorization checks.

After all functional gates pass, complete and merge legitimate PR135 and any required dependent work, push accepted changes, build immutable artifacts, deploy through the authorized process, and record actual public URLs, component SHAs, health, exposure and rollout receipts without spending Mainnet funds.

Test that invalid/missing evidence causes a nonzero exit before mutation, that a valid accepted candidate progresses, that concurrent identity drift fails, and that emergency rollback to a previously accepted version is not blocked by a new candidate's failed evidence.

title: Restore required authority integrations with truthful readiness
cause: The live source documents show multiple unconfigured, stale, degraded and unreachable required authorities, including ord-dogecoin 1404740 blocks behind at the recorded observation. Observations prove prerequisites are missing or unhealthy, but do not distinguish every indexing stall from valid catch-up or establish the private root cause.
decision: Repair the shared owning source configuration/authority before downstream UI. Preserve valid indexing, exact quantity/identity semantics and unavailable-versus-empty distinction. Do not invent a source-level defect from lag alone.
steps: Use the source status snapshots and protocol matrix to enumerate every dependent reader. For each unconfigured authority, reconcile the actual deployed service and its owned health/checkpoint/data routes against PROTOCOL_FEED_ROUTES or PROTOCOL_OBJECT_ROUTES before adding configuration. Require its correct context, supported operation set and credentials through the existing secret store.

For stale/degraded authorities, take successive checkpoint height/hash/timestamp observations, compare the same height with the owned node, inspect targeted bounded service logs and progress/resource metrics, and distinguish valid catch-up/reorg from an actual stall. Do not raise the 144-block threshold, overwrite checkpoints, stop active valid indexers or infer complete history from tip proximity.

When a concrete cause is established, implement at the real ingestion/reader/checkpoint owner in an isolated worktree preserving dirty concurrent work. Record schema/backfill impact and add its file-local instructions before changing it. Reuse shared ord/reference services rather than deploy duplicate competing indexers.

Keep pagination type and identifier encodings exact for each authority. Treat empty answers as proven-empty only when that authority actually answered with sufficient evidence; retain missing-reader, timeout, partial coverage and unknown reference states independently.

Retest each dependent protocol operation including collection pagination, detail reads, outpoints/transactions/holdings where offered, reorg/restart recovery and consumer refresh. Produce actual supported test-network evidence, not readiness-only passes.

title: Resolve actual runtime and validation prerequisites without bypassing security
cause: The documented D:/universe.ssh/config path does not exist; D:/universe/.ssh/config exists but direct reading returned EPERM, and OpenSSH BatchMode with it exited 255 with no diagnostic output. Runtime service configuration, database state and indexer logs were therefore not verified. Two Node release tests also failed because python3 was absent; this is a local test prerequisite, separate from the three real matrix failures.
decision: Use existing approved runtime access or restore the authorized connection through the established operator process, without reading/exporting credentials, changing ACLs to bypass a boundary or resetting secrets. Resolve test tooling in an isolated audit directory, never by changing a production indexer's Python runtime.
steps: Attempt the established approved SSH/service management path with noninteractive authentication and a bounded timeout. Capture a useful sanitized connection error. If the current process identity cannot use the approved key/config, preserve the exact access prerequisite and use an authorized execution context; do not bypass protections or ask to rotate credentials.

Once connected, record readlink component targets, service active state and version identities, safe network/listener information, source configuration presence/context only, node/indexer checkpoints and bounded redacted logs. Do not dump environment files, wallets or credentials. Compare successive indexer observations before deciding a worker stalled.

Use one existing application port and a dedicated browser context; avoid duplicate workers/indexers/frontend processes. Record each dependency's private runtime revision independently from local and GitHub commits.

For the missing Python test helper, use a verified isolated interpreter or the established Linux self-hosted test environment; prepend its path only to that validation process. Do not change Stamps or any consensus-sensitive production Python environment.

Repeat only checks blocked by the repaired prerequisite, retain the initial failure record and record new environment/version. Access limitations remain BLOCKED rather than assumed implementation faults.

title: Close exact protocol/specification and authority-contract gaps
cause: The request spans 39 protocol identities and existing advanced tools. Authoritative sources are available for shared Bitcoin/Ord/Runes/HTTP and several reference implementations, but complete deployed-version, protocol-specific semantics and supported-network proof have not been established for every authority or bespoke protocol. An accessible local repository is not evidence its code is the governing specification or current production revision.
decision: Reuse the pinned source register and repository baselines; perform targeted missing specification/implementation checks only. Do not invent semantics, add competitor products or conduct another undirected broad audit.
steps: For every protocol operation, pin the governing specification or normative reference implementation and the exact authority build. Runes behavior is defined by ord code, not the prose guide; inspect the deployed/pinned ord implementation and its network activation/deciphering/reorg tests.

For every bespoke protocol, inspect the recorded owning repository's versioned protocol documentation and authority parser/read contract; record explicitly whether it is normative, reference behavior or an unresolved external requirement. Do not infer ownership, lifecycle, decimal precision or network support from marketing names.

Resolve transaction identifiers, pagination, quantity precision, ownership interpretation, incomplete-history behavior, checkpoint/hash provenance, confirmation/reorg semantics and restart recovery for each reader. Carry the exact operation-to-source-to-code-to-test mapping into the acceptance matrix.

Study protocol-specific supported test-network parameters and activation. Bitcoin Signet is preferred when supported; Dogecoin/Zcash/Fractal require their own implementation-supported test networks. Local deterministic vectors are complementary evidence, not a substitute for the real network journeys the operation requires.

Reconcile authoritative disagreements at the applicable pinned version. Retain unresolved gaps with the next exact file/symbol/network check and its decision rule; never promote their dependent rows to PASS. Add file-local instructions in an authority worktree only once a concrete change and cause are known.
tests: Protocol-owned conformance/test-vector suites and owned-authority readback paths named in research/source-register.json and inventory/protocol-operation-matrix.json; commands not yet executed are explicitly unverified
Repeat targeted research only for a concrete version drift or uncovered semantic/network requirement
acceptance: Every required operation has sufficient versioned authoritative grounding and executable assertions without invented semantics; all deployed dependency versions and network rules are bound to the accepted evidence.
rollback: No speculative migrations, protocol activation or authority replacement. Preserve exact prior references and valid test evidence while resolving new gaps.

annotations.local: 1. Retain the 39 published protocol identities while binding each operation to its actual authority, governing specification revision and supported execution contexts in the acceptance artifact. 2. Keep historical readable/coverage declarations separate from present readability and functional proof. 3. For bespoke/unsupported-network gaps, follow the exact owning repository references and record unresolved requirements instead of guessing semantics or excluding broken features. 4. Extend manifest specs to reject lost operation identities and mismatched acceptance bindings after WP01/WP03; run the registry suite and existing exporter verification without fabricating PASS records.
